The answer depends on what type of "first railway" is meant, as the retrieved evidence covers several distinct milestones. The earliest railway-like structures, wooden-railed "wagonways," existed as early as 1550 in Germany [d6]. The first public railway (edgeway) was the Lake Lock Rail Road, built in 1796 [d2]. The Stockton and Darlington Railway in England, which opened on September 27, 1825, is recognized as the first railway in the world to operate freight and passenger service with steam traction [d3][d7]. In the Americas, the first railroad track — a military "gravity road" — was built in 1764 in Lewiston, New York [d9][d2], while the first chartered and built railroad in the United States was the Granite Railway of Massachusetts (1826) [d4].
